To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) postoperative radiotherapy is associated with a reduction in biochemical failure and local recurrence, and an improvement in overall survival in patients with pT3 disease; (ii) postoperative radio therapy is associated with a reduced risk of metastatic disease, and an improvement of overall survival in patients who have a high risk of recurrence; (iii) postoperative radio-therapy is associated with an improved overall survival in patients at intermediate risk of recurrence.

(1) adjuvant and early salvage radiotherapy are equally effective for preventing biochemical recurrence in men with high-risk prostate cancer treated with radical prostatectomy; and (2) there is insufficient evidence to recommend adjuvant radiotherapy over salvage radiotherapy for preventing overall mortality.
